source: DHM Islamic Studies Level 2 · lesson 27. Exercises reused from the lesson.
topic: Giving purifies our wealth and our hearts

learn.en: The first meaning of zakah is purity and cleanliness. Giving part of our wealth to the poor and needy purifies it.
learn.title: Purity

learn.en: In English it is called alms, poor-due or poor-tax — but “purifying dues” fits best, because giving cleans our wealth and our inner self.
learn.title: Purifying dues

learn.en: A rich person who refuses zakah is selfish and not thankful to Allah, who gave him more than he needs.
learn.title: Not selfish

learn.en: Zakah is a test from Allah, and the third pillar of Islam.
learn.title: The third pillar

learn.en: “Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and cause them increase.” (Qur'an 9:103)
learn.title: From the Qur'an

quiz.en: The first meaning of zakah is…
Zakah is the ___ pillar of Islam.
True or false? Giving purifies our inner self too.

think.q: Even before you must pay zakah, how could you give some of your pocket money to someone in need?
think.a: A little sadaqah from your own money is a beautiful start.

parents.summary: Zakah means purity: giving part of our wealth purifies it and us; refusing it is selfish; it is the third pillar.
parents.tip: Set up a small sadaqah jar for his pocket money.
